Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Godot transport adapters

1 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

Import transportgd "godot:replay/godot/transport" when owning a raw Godot transport. These adapters implement the engine-free tr.Transport contract and keep sockets, engine references, packet buffers, and callbacks outside the gameplay world.

The normal Session, Room, and Party owners open their own backends. Use this package for a directly owned transport, a control-service listener, or explicit backend configuration.

Backend Owner Setup Transport view
Native UDP Enet enet_host / enet_join enet_transport
WebRTC data channels Rtc rtc_open with Rtc_Config rtc_transport
WebSocket messages Websocket websocket_host / websocket_join websocket_transport
GodotSteam Steam steam_open with Steam_Config and an initialized Steam_Runtime steam_transport
An existing Godot peer Multiplayer_Transport multiplayer_attach multiplayer_transport

Keep the owner at a stable address until closed. A tr.Transport is a borrowed view; copying the view does not transfer or duplicate ownership. Poll the view once per frame, receive packets into caller storage, and close it before discarding the owner:

Odin
import transportgd "godot:replay/godot/transport"
import tr "godot:replay/transport"

host_example :: proc() -> bool {
	peer: transportgd.Enet
	if !transportgd.enet_host(&peer, 4242) {return false}
	wire := transportgd.enet_transport(&peer)
	// Drive tr.poll, tr.send, and tr.receive while peer remains alive.
	tr.close(&wire)
	return true
}

The adapters own or retain the Godot references documented by their setup procedures. They do not install a scene tree's MultiplayerAPI, so engine RPCs and scene multiplayer remain a separate owner. WebSocket text messages use websocket_send_text / websocket_receive; its generic transport view carries binary reliable messages.

RTC setup, authorization, ICE settings, continuation data, and peer identities stay together here. Steam setup and endpoint conversion likewise share this package. These feature-package imports use the same packet formats, identity encoding, authority policies and supported backends as the lifecycle package.
